sentences.text: Microsoft just built a Surface laptop that can cost almost 6,000.
And somehow, the price isn't even the craziest part.
Microsoft teamed up with Nvidia to build the new Surface laptop Ultra,
powered by Nvidia's new RTX Spark Chip.
And this is very different from your normal laptop GPU.
Instead of having regular RAM over here and separate graphics memory over there,
the CPU and Nvidia GPU can share the same pool.
of memory.
Microsoft offers up to 128 gigabytes of it.
Now, that does not mean you're getting an Nvidia graphics card with 128 gigs of VRAM.
The actual GPU is a Blackwell RTX GPU with up to 6,144 CUDA cores.
But because it can access that huge shared memory pool,
it can handle workloads that normally wouldn't even fit into a laptop GPU's memory.
And that's where things gets.
Nvidia says RTX Spark delivers up to one petaflop of AI performance,
and can run AI models with around 120 billion parameters locally.
As in, on your laptop.
No giant desktop workstation, no sending the entire model to the cloud.
And Microsoft didn't exactly put all of this inside a giant brick, either.
You get a 15-inch mini LED touchscreen, up to 2,000 nits HDR brightness,
a full-size SD card reader, HDMI, USB-A, and USBC,
all in a laptop weighing under 4.5 pounds.
They even made the USBC charger magnetic.
But then there's the price.
The Surface Laptop Ultra starts at $2,599.
And if you want that ridiculous 128 gigabyte configuration, you're looking at $5,899.99.
So, yeah.
Microsoft basically built a portable Nvidia AI workstation and disguised it as a surface laptop.
The only question is, who actually needs this much laptop?
